title: Lesson Plan — The Rise of Nationalism in Europe (Class 10 CBSE History)
subject: Social Science (History)
chapter_title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
objectives: Explain the impact of the French Revolution and Napoleonic Code on European nationalism.
Describe the role of the educated middle class and Romanticism in spreading nationalism.
Trace the major liberal-nationalist uprisings of 1830 and 1848.
Outline the unification of Germany and Italy.
Identify and interpret female allegories (Marianne, Germania) of European nations.
Explain how late-19th-century nationalism led to the Balkan conflict and the First World War.
prerequisites: Familiarity with the French Revolution from Class 9 History.
A basic grasp of the political map of 18th- and 19th-century Europe.
Comfort reading source extracts and visuals.
materials: Printed copy of Frédéric Sorrieu's 1848 print (textbook image)
Outline maps of Europe before and after 1871
A timeline strip (1789 → 1914) for the wall
Worksheet — Rise of Nationalism in Europe

activities.description: Show Sorrieu's 1848 print on the board. Ask: 'What is being celebrated here? Who are the figures? Why is the central figure a woman?' Take guesses; promise the lesson will explain.
student_actions: Note one question of their own.

activities.description: On a 1789 → 1914 timeline strip, students place pre-printed cards: French Revolution, Napoleonic Code, Greek independence, July Revolution, 1848 revolutions, Italian unification, German unification, World War I.

Cover four blocks: (i) French Revolution + Napoleonic Code; (ii) middle class + Romanticism + folk culture + 1830/1848; (iii) unification of Italy and Germany; (iv) allegories + late nationalism + Balkans.
teacher_actions: Sketch a simple map of Europe c. 1815.
Explain Marianne and Germania with the print.
student_actions: Mark new states on the outline maps.
Repeat the names of leaders (Bismarck, Cavour, Garibaldi, Mazzini).

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering definitions, dates, leaders, allegories and a short-answer on 1848.
Exit ticket: 4 quick questions, one from each block.
Homework: read the section on the Balkans again; sketch a short paragraph on why those conflicts led to WWI.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (Nationalism in India).

homework: Make a chronological table of major events 1789–1914 with one-line significance for each.
Sketch and label the female allegories Marianne (France) and Germania (Germany).
Write one paragraph on why the Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 failed.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the shift from liberal to imperialist nationalism using the rubric.
references: NCERT Class 10 — India and the Contemporary World – II, Chapter 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe.
